title: 3 months of running Claude + agentic Robinhood
author: Abject_Disaster7292
selftext:
I’ve been experimenting with an agentic Robinhood setup using Claude for the past 3 months, and so far it’s been a pretty solid run. We’re up **5.93% over the past 3 months**.  
We initially started with **$1,000**, and the beginning was definitely a little rocky. After a few rounds of optimization, we increased the budget to **$2,000**. We’ve been making adjustments as we collect more data, and performance has picked up significantly along the way.  
I’ve mostly vibe-coded the system, and Claude is currently handling the trades fully autonomously without me needing to manually approve or engage with each trade.  
Still an experiment, obviously, but it’s been pretty cool to watch it evolve as we feed it more data and optimize the approach.

comments.author: Abject_Disaster7292
comments.body:
For all the gatekeeping wack ass haters questioning my approach — this is not a fraudulent post. Here is 50% of my exact playbook.

**What you need**

* Robinhood account with agentic/API access enabled (Account → Settings)
* Claude Code installed (claude.ai/code) — this is Anthropic's CLI, not the web chatbot
* A dedicated folder on your computer for your trading files

**Step 1 — Connect the MCP**

This is the one line that makes everything possible. Run this in Claude Code from your trading folder:

`claude mcp add robinhood-trading --transport http` [`https://agent.robinhood.com/mcp/trading`](https://agent.robinhood.com/mcp/trading)

Claude can now check positions, get quotes, place orders, set stops, and cancel orders through a conversation. Verify it worked by asking "what's my account balance?" in a new session.

**Step 2 — Pick your sectors and build your watchlist manually**

This part is on you. Claude doesn't randomly scan the whole market — you tell it which sectors and themes you're watching, and you curate the tickers. I manually input the sectors I believe in (AI infrastructure, semiconductors, defense, energy) and specific names within those I want tracked. Claude then monitors those names during scans, not the entire market.

The adjacency matters too. If I'm watching GPU stocks I'm also watching the power infrastructure plays around them. You build that logic yourself and feed it in. This is where your own conviction lives — Claude executes it, it doesn't replace it.

**Step 3 — Write your rules in** [**CLAUDE.md**](http://CLAUDE.md)

Create a [CLAUDE.md](http://CLAUDE.md) file in your trading folder. Claude loads this automatically in every session. Define at minimum:

* Position sizing (I target $1,000/position, whole shares only)
* Entry criteria
* Stop-loss percentage
* Profit targets and how you scale out
* A no-chase rule (don't enter if already up X% from prior close)
* An explicit autonomy grant — tell Claude it can execute trades without asking permission first

The autonomy grant is non-negotiable. If Claude has to ask you before every trade you've built a chatbot, not a system.

**Step 4 — Start a trading log**

Make a logs/ folder. Each day gets its own file. Claude writes to it during scans and reads it before each new one — this stops it from re-analyzing tickers it already rejected earlier in the day.

**Step 5 — Run manually first**

Run sessions by hand for at least a week before automating. Open Claude Code and say something like "screen my watchlist for setups, check my positions, execute anything that qualifies." Watch what it does. Fix your rules when it makes a bad call. Don't automate until you trust the rules.

**Step 6 — Set up scheduled scans**

Claude Code has a scheduled tasks system. Once your rules are solid, create scan agents that fire throughout the day: pre-market, market open, mid-morning, midday, power hour, close. Each one runs your rules against live data and acts automatically.

**Step 7 — Build your memory**

There's a persistent memory system at \~/.claude/projects/\[your-dir\]/memory/. Write memory files for lessons learned, rule refinements after bad trades, and known account limitations. Every future session loads these automatically — the system gets smarter over time.

**What I'd tell myself at the start**

Rules over gut. When you want to override mid-trade, update the rule for next time instead.

Audit live positions directly, not just the log. The log can miss trades from interrupted scans.

Whole shares only. Fractional shares break stop-loss orders on some account types.

The biggest unlock is autonomy. A system that checks with you on every trade isn't autonomous. Trust your rules or fix your rules, but don't half-commit.

Compounding is slow. +5% in a quarter on $2k isn't impressive in dollar terms. The rules and the system you're building are the actual asset.
